title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the reconstruction begun on p.59 and does two things.

**(i) The order relation and its nerve.** A strict order relation on the points of Σ has already been extracted from the data. Here Grothendieck records how the data are recovered from that order, formula (39):
- Σ*(1) is the graph of the strict order, {(x<y)}, with p1 = s (source) : (x<y) ↦ x and b (but, target) : (x<y) ↦ y.
- Σ*(2) is the space of 2-flags (x<y<z), with three maps:
  - p2 : (x<y<z) ↦ (x,y)
  - s' : (x<y<z) ↦ (x,z)
  - b' : (x<y<z) ↦ (y,z)

In modern terms Σ ⇇ Σ*(1) ⇇ Σ*(2) is the 2-truncated nerve of a topological poset, with the face maps named as follows:
- s = d1 and b = d0 on 1-simplices;
- p2 = d2, s' = d1 and b' = d0 on 2-simplices.

**(ii) The Scholie.** It axiomatizes the situation by three pieces of data.
1. A topological space Σ with a (pre)cylindrical stratification. Σ1 is the space of codimension-1 strata, so that b : Σ*(1) → Σ is a proper 'bordant' (boundary-type) immersion, i.e. the normalization of the union of codimension-1 boundary pieces.
2. An order on Σ, given locally: for each x in b(Σ1), a total order on the codimension-1 strata passing through x. This is subject to the condition that the order is given by a closed part Σ*(2) of the fibre product Σ*(1) ×_Σ Σ*(1). This yields the diagram Σ*(2) ⇉ Σ*(1) → Σ.
3. A continuous map p1 = s : Σ*(1) → Σ (the projection of the cylindrical structure). Condition (a): (s,b) : Σ*(1) → Σ×Σ is injective and misses the diagonal, i.e. s(u) ≠ b(u).

The next page completes the axioms:
- (b) Segal-type condition: Σ*(2) → Σ×Σ factors through Σ*(1), giving p2, and the square (b', p2 ; p1, b) is cartesian. That is, Σ*(2) = Σ*(1) ×_{b,Σ,p1} Σ*(1).
- Transversality of p1 to the boundary immersion b.
- Conclusion: equivalently, the structure is a Hausdorff space with an order relation whose strict graph is closed and whose target map b is a proper bordant immersion.

The purpose is to encode the combinatorics of a cylindrically stratified space (part of the 'déploiement' programme, resolving a stratified space by a manifold-with-corners-like object) as a topological poset or simplicial space. The cylindrical projections then compose transitively.
errors: The Scholie says 'relation d'ordre total' on Σ. The global relation is only a partial order; it is total only on the set of codimension-1 strata through a given point. The next page corrects this to 'relation d'ordre'.

In (39) the second components of s' and b' were first written wrongly and then corrected (crossed letters in the image). The final version s'=(x,z), b'=(y,z), p2=(x,y) is consistent. Check: p1 s' = p1 p2, b s' = b b', and b p2 = p1 b'. The cartesian square then identifies Σ*(2) with composable pairs (x<y),(y<z).
Condition 2° is stated loosely: 'partie fermée Σ*(2) de (Σ*(1) ×_Σ (Σ*(1),b) ...)' is unfinished. The closedness and Segal conditions are only made precise on the next page.
No real mathematical error otherwise. Irreflexivity (image misses the diagonal) plus transitivity (p.59) correctly gives a strict order, and antisymmetry follows.

ideas.what: Recovering the stratification combinatorics as the nerve of a topological strict order: Σ*(1) = graph of <, Σ*(2) = 2-flags, with face maps s, b, p2, s', b'.
ideas.modern_name: Nerve of a topological poset / 2-truncated simplicial space (topological category with object space Σ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nerves of topological categories: Segal (1968). Stratified spaces as topological posets or exit-path categories: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (Higher Algebra A.6), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017).
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts. Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the 'tame topology / dévissage of stratified spaces' programme.

ideas.what: Axiomatization of a (pre)cylindrical stratification by a proper bordant immersion b : Σ*(1) → Σ together with a projection s : Σ*(1) → Σ, satisfying injectivity of (s,b), disjointness from the diagonal, a cartesian (Segal) square and transversality of s to b.
ideas.modern_name: Control data / tube systems for stratified spaces encoded as a simplicial (Segal-type) space; cf. Mather's control data, manifolds with corners / ⟨n⟩-manifolds (Jänich, Laures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (control data); Jänich (1968) and Laures (2000) for manifolds with faces; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka for conically smooth unzipping.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 mentions 'déploiement' of stratified spaces only programmatically.

ideas.what: Equivalence of the structure with 'a Hausdorff space with a closed order relation such that the target map of the strict graph is a proper bordant immersion'.
ideas.modern_name: Ordered topological space (Nachbin) with an étale/immersive target condition; topological poset model of a stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nachbin (closed-order spaces); exit-path poset models are recent (Lurie, AFT).

missed.claim: Grothendieck encodes the corner/cylindrical structure of a 'deployed' stratified space as a simplicial space Σ ⇇ Σ*(1) ⇇ Σ*(2) satisfying a Segal-type cartesian condition. Its points carry a closed strict order realized geometrically by boundary immersions and collar projections. This anticipates the later viewpoint that stratified spaces with conical or cylindrical data are equivalent to certain topological or ∞-categorical poset-like structures (exit-path categories, AFT 'unzipping' to manifolds with corners). Here the poset lives on the points of the resolved space, not on the set of strata.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A pointwise topological-poset formulation of corner/collar data could give an alternative, elementary model for the unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces. It is not clearly present in that form in the Ayala–Francis–Tanaka or Lurie literature. The idea is, however, only partially worked out here.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is a careful but essentially routine recognition that the data form the nerve of a topological strict order with a Segal condition. The geometric axiomatization of cylindrical stratifications via a proper bordant immersion plus a transversal projection is of some historical interest as an early categorical/simplicial encoding of stratification data. Its content is close to known notions: control data, manifolds with corners, exit-path posets.
transcription_corrections: Line 1° should read 'immersion bordante propre' (consistent with the next page), not 'immersion bord[?] propre'.
The top-right diagram has three arrows Σ*(2) → Σ*(1), labelled p2, s', b' (the transcription renders them as two plus one).
In 3°(a) the source is written with a hat or star, Σ^*(1) (as Σ̂(1) in the image), not Σ1.
In 2°, 'sur la base[?] de Σ1' is probably 'sur la base de Σ1' or 'sur les strates de Σ1'. The phrase is 'Une relation d'ordre total relative à Σ1, sur Σ'.
The crossing-outs in (39) are: for s' an initial wrong letter crossed and replaced by x, giving (x,z); for b' a crossed letter replaced by y, giving (y,z).
The margin note is roughly '3 str[atifications] de projections loc[ales] et cylindriques ... ordre ...'; it is illegible in parts.
